Write JSON directly to a file

Source: R/json.R
write_json.Rd

The document is written incrementally. Its total size may exceed 2 GB; the input R object must still fit in R memory. For generated batches, use jsonlite::stream_out().

Usage

write_json(
  x,
  path,
  dataframe = c("rows", "columns", "values"),
  auto_unbox = FALSE,
  na = c("null", "string"),
  factor = c("string", "integer"),
  always_decimal = FALSE,
  pretty = FALSE,
  digits = NA
)

Arguments

x

An atomic vector, array, list, or data frame. Array dimensions are written in their existing order, including dimensions of length one or zero.

path

Destination file path.

dataframe

Data frame layout: rows, columns, or values.

auto_unbox

Whether length-one atomic vectors become scalars.

na

Encode missing and non-finite values as JSON null or as strings.

factor

Encode factors as level labels ("string", the default) or integer level indices ("integer").

always_decimal

Distinguish doubles from integers by retaining a decimal point or exponent in finite double output.

pretty

Whether to indent JSON with two spaces per level. Pretty file output ends with a newline.

digits

Must be NA. Numbers retain full round-trip precision; rounding to a specified number of digits is not implemented.

Value

The path, invisibly.

Details

The document is first written to a temporary file in the directory of path and moved into place once it is complete, so an existing file at path is left untouched when writing fails.

See also

jsonlite::read_json() to read the file back, jsonlite::stream_out() for newline-delimited JSON.

Examples

path <- tempfile(fileext = ".json")
write_json(data.frame(id = 1:3, name = c("A", "B", "C")), path)
readLines(path, warn = FALSE)
#> [1] "[{\"id\":1,\"name\":\"A\"},{\"id\":2,\"name\":\"B\"},{\"id\":3,\"name\":\"C\"}]"
read_json(path)
#>   id name
#> 1  1    A
#> 2  2    B
#> 3  3    C
unlink(path)
